arcade-after-hours:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: purpose-designed thin OBS overlay frame, landscape 16:9, 1920x1080 if possible, transparent RGBA PNG. Reference image 1 shows the APPROVED FRAME WEIGHT and use: a very thin bespoke rim with an irregular organic inner edge and almost entirely empty transparent middle. Reference image 2 is STYLE AND THEME INSPIRATION only; do not crop it. Design a NEW frame individually for this theme, do not merely recolor reference 1. Maintain roughly 85–90 percent truly transparent canvas. Artwork hugs the very outer perimeter. Most runs are 2–3% of canvas height deep, small corner features may reach 5% at most. Gentle non-linear inside silhouette made by small purposeful steps, bends, protrusions and gaps. Every motif must be miniature and integrated in the narrow rim; NO large panels, labels, interior scenery or thick bottom bar. Razor-sharp high fidelity pixel art, rich detailed pixel shading. No blur, no soft haze spilling into middle. Actual alpha transparency in center and around irregular contours, NOT black fill or painted checkerboard. No text or watermark. One complete thin frame viewed straight on.
Theme: ARCADE AFTER HOURS revision 2. Invent a thin midnight-blue arcade/pinball frame inspired by the second image's neon city, star-lit arcade cabinets and pinball machines. Small cyan/magenta luminous rails bend around tiny gold pinball bumpers, miniature joystick/button accents at two corners, a few pixel stars or tiny space-invader symbols embedded in the rim. A little checkered/racing trim and miniature illuminated cabinet vent details. Cobalt/navy base, blue and hot-pink trim, warm gold highlights. The frame should look like a whimsical premium arcade fascia, NOT the brass industrial Pac-Man frame. Center entirely transparent, no skyline or sky filling it.

pacman-maze.initial:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one purpose-designed OBS overlay border, a transparent PNG, landscape 16:9 ideally 1920x1080.
Input image: STYLE REFERENCE ONLY for materials, pixel-art fidelity, color, arcade electronics. Do NOT crop or punch a rectangular hole in the reference. Design a NEW frame specifically for live OBS content.
Primary request: an extremely THIN, beautifully crafted Pac-Man arcade machinery frame hugging the very outside of the canvas, with a huge genuinely transparent center. Approximately 90% of the canvas area should remain transparent and usable for live screen/camera content.
Style: crisp high-fidelity pixel art matching the reference, dark navy metal, scuffed warm brass, small luminous cyan blue maze tubes, subtle amber/red indicator lights, fine discrete pixel highlights. Sharp pixels, no blur or photographic smooth shading.
Composition: all artwork constrained to a narrow rim roughly 2–3% of frame height on straight stretches; a few small corner details may reach 5% inward at most. Much THINNER and more restrained than the reference. No giant panels or bulky bottom bar. Make the INNER SILHOUETTE gently irregular and hand-designed, NOT one straight rectangular cutout: tiny cable bends, staggered circuit boards, pipe elbows, a few chip tabs and subtle pixel-stepped silhouettes create a coherent varied edge. Small asymmetrical groupings alternate with very slim quiet runs. The cyan tube follows this irregular architecture instead of drawing a second inset rectangle. Tiny integrated Pac-Man/pellet motifs in the rim, not large floating characters. Nothing chopped off at a straight inner crop boundary; every element ends in a designed contour.
Transparency: actual alpha transparency for the entire empty center and gaps between protrusions. No background color, no checkerboard painted into image, no interior sign, no solid glass panel, no vignette, no shadow or glow washing across the transparent center.
No text, no words, no labels, no logo, no mockup UI. Straight-on orthographic full-canvas frame, no perspective. The main clear central rectangle from x=5% to95%, y=5%to95% must be completely empty alpha. Exactly one finished frame asset.
pacman-maze.approved_thinning_pass:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit this transparent OBS overlay frame. Keep its existing 1672x941 landscape canvas, palette, crisp pixel art, Pac-Man machine identity and organically stepped inner silhouette. Preserve true alpha transparency.
Make the ENTIRE BORDER roughly HALF as thick everywhere, including all corners, top and bottom, and side modules. This is for a live content overlay and the current border is still too heavy. Re-design the components smaller/slimmer rather than chopping them at a straight cut line. Keep the outer edge at the canvas perimeter and move the irregular inner edge much closer to it. Target at least 88 percent fully transparent canvas. Straight runs only 15–22 pixels deep on top/bottom and 18–28 pixels wide on sides; occasional tiny cable bends or corner fixtures can reach 35–40 pixels inward, but no more. The empty central area should overwhelmingly dominate. Keep only two small Pac-Man motifs total, reduce repeated plaques and vents. Small precise blue tubes, tiny brass fasteners, thin cables, a few tasteful small LEDs. Preserve the irregular shape: a few short stepped tabs, rounded pipe bends and cable loops, never a straight rectangular cutout. No new solid inner outline, no interior shadow/haze/glow, no background/checkerboard, no text. Output one exceptionally thin bespoke frame with completely transparent interior.
